title: Your exit and risk rules
desc: Set your stop, target, size and daily and weekly loss limits before you buy

cards.title: How many shares?
cards.situation: Your account is $10,000 and you risk 1% a trade. You buy at $50 with a stop at $48. How many shares?

options.feedback: 200 shares would lose about $400 at the stop. That’s 4% of your account on one trade.
If the stop is hit, you lose about $100, your 1%. A gap overnight or on earnings can cost more.
100 shares would lose about $200 at the stop. That’s 2% of your account, double your 1%.

cards.title: Decide the exit before you enter
cards.text: Every trade needs three numbers **before** you buy: where you get out if wrong, where you take profit, and how big to go.

blocks.tip: Buy at $50. Risk $2 a share to make $4. A [[stop-loss|stop]] limits the loss. It doesn’t guarantee the price.

cards.title: Loss limits: the circuit breaker
cards.text: On $10,000: stop for the day at −2% ($200). Stop for the week at −5% ($500).

items.label: Mon −$100, Tue −$200 day limit hit, Wed −$100, Thu −$100 week limit hit

rows.note: −$200 is your 2% for the day. Close the app. Week so far: −$300.
A new day, a new $200 limit. Week so far: −$400.
Week so far: −$500, your 5%. No more trades this week.

items.label: The week’s losses reach the −$500 limit

cards.foot: Week total hits −$500 on Thursday. No more trades until Monday. Limits stop a bad day becoming a bad month.

cards.title: Aim for at least 2× the risk
cards.text: Risk $100 to make **$200** or more. Then you can be wrong more often than right and still come out ahead.

visual.label: 4 winners make $800, 6 losers lose $600: 10 trades net +$200

blocks.tip: Before costs. Fees and slippage eat into this, so the target must be worth the trip.

cards.title: One more trade?
cards.q: Your rule: risk no more than 2% ($200) a day. You’ve lost $150 today. A new trade would risk $100. Take it?

options.feedback: A good setup doesn’t change the limit.

options.text: No: it would take you past $200 today
options.feedback: $150 lost plus $100 more at risk could make $250, past your $200 limit. You’re done for today.

options.text: Yes, with double size to win it back
options.feedback: Doubling size to win it back is how a bad day becomes a bad month. The limit says stop.

options.text: Yes, if you move the stop further away
options.feedback: A wider stop risks even more. The limit counts what you could lose, and it says stop.

cards.title: Near the stop
cards.q: Your trade is close to the stop. You want to move the stop lower “to give it room”. What does your plan say?

options.text: Move it: the price will come back
options.feedback: Moving the stop turns a 1% loss into a bigger one. You set it with a clear head. Keep it.

options.text: Keep it where you set it before entry
options.feedback: You set the stop with a clear head, before you bought. Leave it, and the loss stays near 1%.
With no stop, there’s no limit to the loss. Your plan says the stop stays where you set it.

options.text: Buy more to lower your average price
options.feedback: Buying more near the stop makes a losing trade bigger. The stop stays where you set it.

cards.headline: Your risk has a ceiling.
lines: Risk 1% a trade: shares = risk ÷ (entry − stop).
Stop and target are set before you buy.
Stop for the day at −2%, for the week at −5%.
